subject: Audit request: chain of custody for VPC log exports

From: Alex Burke <alex.burke@globex.com>

Cc: audit@globex.com
Date: 2025-04-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: chain-of-custody evidence for private VPC deploy

Hi Ben,

We have a scheduled compliance review with our SOC team next Tuesday. They need a clear chain-of-custody for the logs and traces that Redwood ships out of our private VPC deployment — specifically: what is logged locally, what gets forwarded, how long temporary artifacts (e.g., evidence bundles, intermediate archives) are retained, and the control points where signatures/hashes are applied.

Would you be able to provide an evidence packet or checklist we can present? A manifest CSV and a signed acknowledgement (DocuSign) would be ideal. If useful, we can do a short call to run through the packet.

Thanks,
Alex Burke
CIO, Globex Corporation

Alex —

Thanks for the heads up. We can assemble a compliance packet that covers:
- Local log/trace capture points inside the customer VPC (collector sidecars, forwarder service)
- In-transit protections (mTLS, signed handshakes, egress ACLs)
- Evidence bundle creation process (timestamping, manifest.csv, SHA256 checksums)
- Short-lived artifacts and retention windows (what we keep temporarily during packaging)
- Delivery points (S3/HEC endpoint or Splunk/Partner) and final residency
- Roles that attest to the bundle (Redwood engineer + customer security approver)

I'll attach an initial draft manifest and a PDF summary. Kimberly, can you validate the signing/packaging checklist and add any required tracehook details? Marissa — looping you for the call scheduling and DocuSign routing.

We can have a formal packet by EOD tomorrow if that works for your audit cadence.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Kimberly — forwarding Alex's request. Short checklist below (please paste updates inline):

1) Collector & Forwarder proofs
   - Collector runs on host with file-based buffering; forwarder signs bundles with node key before upload.
   - Are we generating a per-bundle SHA256 and embedding it in the manifest?
2) Packaging flow
   - Evidence bundle includes logs, matching trace index, manifest.csv, and packer metadata.json.
   - Temporary archive retention is 72 hours on the packer pod; then uploaded and removed.
3) In-transit and endpoint control
   - mTLS to customer-managed HEC/S3, enforced via TLS policies and egress ACLs.
4) Attestation
   - Internal: engineer who triggered bundle (name + email).
   - External: customer security owner signs DocuSign after review.

Alex asked for a signed acknowledgement. Can we generate the audit_manifest_signature.pdf after you confirm the signing fields and hash flow? Also, add any tracehook specifics (span sampling rules, downstream id mapping) we should include in the packet.

Thanks — Ben

Alex / Ben —

I've reviewed the packaging flow and completed the checklist. Summary of updates we will include in the final packet: 

- Bundle hashing: every evidence bundle will include a manifest.csv with per-file SHA256 and overall bundle SHA256. The manifest is generated by the packer process (packerd) and stored as plaintext in the bundle root.
- Timestamping: packerd records an ISO8601 create_time and also writes a signed timestamp token (RFC 3161 style) into the packer metadata.json.
- Retention policy: temporary artifacts retained on packer pod for up to 72 hours; if upload fails, artifacts are kept for retry window (additional 48 hours) before auto-expunge.
- Transit: mTLS enforced using customer CA; mutual verification at the forwarder endpoint. We will include the TLS cert fingerprint used in the upload handshake in the manifest.
- Trace hooks: for the packet we will include a trace index file that maps bundle content to spans; sampling rules and service-name mapping documented.
- Attestation/signature: I've prepared audit_manifest_signature.pdf that shows the bundle hash, packer node id, and an attestation line for the Redwood on-call engineer. We will also produce a DocuSign envelope for the customer security approver to sign.

Attachments attached to this message: evidence_bundle_v1.zip (zip, sample bundle), audit_manifest_signature.pdf (pdf).

Marissa — please send Alex the Drive folder link and DocuSign envelope; Alex, let us know who on your team will sign so we can pre-fill the envelope.

-Kimberly Park
Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
